kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: Inflation sizzled in September — and Social Security benefits will get a boost
wire.summary: Consumer prices in September jumped 3.7% from a year ago. The Social Security Administration said benefits will increase next year to help keep pace with the rising cost of living.

wire.title: Hands-on with the Ocarina of Time remake, the most ornate Zelda game ever made
wire.summary: We got to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time early. Here are our impressions of the remake and its elaborate new style.

wire.title: Zelenskyy sits down with NPR. And, Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer
wire.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has a sit-down interview with NPR as Russia's full-scale invasion nears the 5-year mark. And, Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer.

wire.title: These workers help train robots who could one day steal their jobs
wire.summary: Factory workers in India are being asked to wear GoPro cameras to record the way they do their jobs. The ultimate goal is to train robots to take over. Will it work?

wire.title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
wire.summary: The White House publicly asked for U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation on Tuesday as she faced mounting accusations of improper conduct.

wire.title: In Kansas, a newly competitive Senate race tests limit of Trump's unpopular policies
wire.summary: Kansas voters could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century — and flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even in what could be a tough year for the GOP.

wire.title: Civil rights advocates plan to send thousands of observers to midterm polling places
wire.summary: For many election cycles, civil rights groups and political parties have fanned out to monitor polling places, but the charged midterm environment has many organizations stepping up efforts this year.

wire.title: 'They're stealing from the poor': A major source of SNAP fraud robs recipients of millions
wire.summary: Organized criminal rings target SNAP recipients because of the government program's outdated security features. But upgrading the tech costs money and states' SNAP budgets are getting squeezed.

wire.title: The skincare scheme that led to consumer complaints, lawsuits and a federal investigation
wire.summary: Free samples, high-pressure pitches and $50,000 bills: An NPR investigation reveals how a network of mall skincare stores systematically targeted older adults and people with disabilities across the U.S.

wire.title: VIDEO: The skincare sample is free. What happens next can cost thousands
wire.summary: For years, customers have complained of aggressive sales tactics and charges at mall skincare stores. NPR investigated the business that connects many of them.

wire.title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says
wire.summary: Elon Musk's system allows Kyiv to protect Ukrainian skies and effectively guide drones to Russian targets.

wire.title: Pope walking and recovering 'as expected' after surgery, doctors say
wire.summary: The 71-year-old Pope was diagnosed with lung cancer after the 90-minute procedure on Tuesday.

wire.title: US inflation rises more than expected - here's what is happening with prices
wire.summary: The pace of price rises increased to 3.7% in the year to September, driving by higher motor fuel costs.

wire.title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
wire.summary: Four years after the attacks, Serhii Kuznetsov appears in court accused of a plot to destroy Russia's gas pipelines to Germany.

wire.title: Australia's first-ever Michelin stars go to 11 restaurants in one state
wire.summary: All of the spots are in South Australia, reportedly because the state government paid for incognito inspectors to visit.

wire.title: Netflix to lay off 1,000 staff in steepest cuts since 2022
wire.summary: The cuts equate to around 6% of the streaming giant's total workforce worldwide.
